Introduction

Getting started

What routiva is, the ideas behind it, and a working server in under a minute.

What is routiva?#

routiva is a small web framework for Node.js that gives you the ergonomics of Express — routing, middleware, request/response helpers, body parsing, static files, CORS, compression, logging and rate limiting — while staying completely dependency-free.

Everything is built on Node's own node:http. There is no path-to-regexp, no body-parser, no mime-types, no transitive tree of packages to audit. The whole framework is roughly 1,900 lines across 17 ES modules.

bash
npm install routiva

Requires Node.js 18 or newer. No runtime dependencies. No dev dependencies.

routiva is not trying to replace Express for everyone. It is for the projects that want a framework small enough to read end to end, and a dependency graph that is exactly node_modules/routiva.

Why another framework?#

Express is excellent, mature and battle-tested. But it carries a large transitive dependency tree and a handful of sharp edges that this project smooths over:

  • Async errors were an afterthought. In Express 4, a rejected promise in a handler hangs the request unless you call next(err) yourself. routiva catches rejected promises and thrown errors automatically.
  • The framework is spread across packages. CORS, compression, rate limiting and MIME types each live in their own dependency. routiva ships them in the core.
  • HTTP correctness is optional. Express returns 404 for a path that exists with the wrong method. routiva answers 405 with an Allow header, and handles OPTIONS and HEAD for you.
  • You cannot read it. Express is many files of which the interesting logic is a fraction. routiva is small enough to understand in an afternoon.

The mental model#

An app is a router. A router is an ordered list of layers. A layer is either a route, a piece of middleware, or an error handler. Requests walk the list top to bottom; the first layer that sends a response ends the journey.

text
incoming request
      │
      ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  layer 0   logger()          → logs, calls next()    │
│  layer 1   cors()            → headers, calls next() │
│  layer 2   json()            → parses body, next()   │
│  layer 3   GET /users/:id    → sends a response  ────┼──▶ done
│  layer 4   error handler     → only runs on next(err)│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

That is the entire design. Once you understand the stack, every other page in these docs is detail.

Your first server#

Create server.js:

js
import { createApp } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();

app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ hello: 'world' });
});

app.get('/users/:id', (req, res) => {
  res.json({ id: req.params.id });
});

app.listen(3000, () => {
  console.log('listening on http://localhost:3000');
});

Run it with node server.js (your package.json should have "type": "module"), then:

bash
curl http://localhost:3000/
curl http://localhost:3000/users/42
